venues.name: Lockhart Bungalow, a CGH Earth SAHA Experience
venues.note: CGH Earth's 1940s planter's bungalow, just three rooms, set within a 1,500-acre working tea estate, looking down on rolling hills and gardens.
credentials: CGH Earth, a SAHA (heritage-home) Experience, the group's Munnar address
Restored 1940s British planter's bungalow, 3 rooms only
Within the ~1,500-acre Lockhart tea estate

venues.name: Windermere Estate
venues.note: An 18-room plantation retreat on a 1940s cardamom-and-coffee estate, high on Observatory Hill, 360-degree views that often look down on the clouds.
credentials: Featured by Scott Dunn, Rare India, Secret Retreats, Kuoni and Audley Travel
18-room estate home on a 1940s cardamom, coffee and tea plantation
Perched on Observatory Hill, in the Palni/Western Ghats

venues.name: Fragrant Nature Munnar
venues.note: A Five Star Classified resort of colonial style over rolling valleys, most of its rooms carry a real in-room fireplace for the cool hill nights.
credentials: Five Star Classified hotel
~43 rooms across five categories, most with authentic in-room fireplaces
Multi-cuisine and speciality dining, spa

venues.name: SpiceTree Munnar
venues.note: The hills' most design-led boutique, 14 suites and two pool villas with solar-heated infinity pools and Victorian copper tubs, each framing forest and valley.
credentials: Award-winning design-led boutique; featured by Wexas Travel (UK luxury operator)
Listed by Kerala Tourism
14 suites + 2 private pool villas with solar-heated infinity pools

venues.name: The Tall Trees Munnar
venues.note: Twenty-six individual cottages scattered across 66 acres of Shola forest under 600-odd towering trees, with a forest restaurant beneath a transparent roof.
credentials: WGH Hotels & Resorts
26 individual cottages across 66 acres of Shola forest
Pool with jacuzzi; glass-roofed forest restaurant

venues.name: Parakkat Nature Hotels & Resorts
venues.note: A large tea-view resort with pool villa suites, a spa and a zipline, Munnar's most decorated crowd-pleaser, over panoramic plantations.
credentials: Tripadvisor Travellers' Choice
~80 rooms from classic to pool villa suites
Spa, multiple pools, panoramic tea-estate views

venues.name: Chandys Windy Woods
venues.note: A quietly chic hillside resort of grey stone and white walls stepped down the slope, muted, calm and plantation-facing.
credentials: Listed by Kerala Tourism
Hillside blocks with mountain-view balconies
Outdoor pool, spa and wellness centre

venues.name: Ambady Estate
venues.note: A handful of split-level chalets and a private villa set within a certified organic cardamom plantation, stone fireplaces and old-world calm.
credentials: Boutique chalets and a private villa within a certified organic cardamom plantation
Two-level chalets with stone fireplaces
Consistently rated for cleanliness and personal service

venues.name: Fragrant Nature Munnar restaurants
venues.note: The hills' most complete resort dining, a multi-cuisine room and a grill speciality restaurant, with valley views and fireplaces.
credentials: In-house dining at a Five Star Classified hotel
Multi-cuisine restaurant plus a speciality grill room

venues.name: Saravana Bhavan, Munnar
venues.note: The Munnar branch of the world's best-known pure-vegetarian South Indian chain, dosas, idlis and filter coffee, done right.
credentials: Branch of the global Saravana Bhavan pure-vegetarian chain
A dependable, veg/Jain-friendly table in the town centre

venues.name: Rapsy Restaurant
venues.note: Munnar's most-recommended local room, famous for parottas, biryani and the day's Kerala plates, packed at lunch with residents.
credentials: Widely cited as Munnar town's best-loved local restaurant (Tripadvisor, Kerala food guides)
Known for parottas, biryani and its multi-country breakfast board

venues.name: SN Restaurant
venues.note: One of Munnar's oldest eating houses, plain, authentic Kerala meals and fish-curry plates in the heart of town.
credentials: One of the oldest established restaurants in Munnar town
Known for authentic, affordable Kerala meals and fish curry

venues.name: Kannan Devan / Tata Tea Museum
venues.note: The story of how the British and then Tata turned these hills into the great Kannan Devan tea country, told inside a working estate, antique rollers, a curling machine, the old Pelton wheel, and a demonstration room where you watch fresh leaf become the cup. A five-minute drive from town and the natural first stop before you set out among the plantations.

venues.name: A private tea-tasting & estate walk (Kannan Devan hills)
venues.note: The rolling emerald plantations that made Munnar famous are best met on foot, a guided walk between the clipped tea bushes at dawn, the pluckers moving through the mist, ending with a proper tasting of single-estate leaf. A concierge arranges a private estate walk with a plantation manager rather than the crowded roadside stops.

venues.name: Tea-plucking with the estate workers
venues.note: A hands-on morning in the gardens, a basket, a guide, and the surprisingly precise 'two leaves and a bud' technique the women pluckers have perfected over generations. Genuinely charming for children and grandparents alike, and the kind of unhurried, grounding experience the luxury tea-bungalows arrange privately for their guests.

venues.name: Kundala Lake & Dam
venues.area: 20 km from Munnar, towards Top Station
venues.note: A quiet high-altitude reservoir cradled by tea slopes and, in season, the rare Neelakurinji, famous for its pedal-boats and a genuinely lovely dawn-and-dusk light on the water. Calmer and less crowded than Mattupetty, it is the one to send a couple to for a slow, misty hour on the lake.

venues.name: Echo Point
venues.area: 15 km from Munnar, towards Top Station
venues.note: A lakeside bend in the hills where a shout comes back to you off the far ridges, a simple, joyful stop that children adore, set on a serene stretch of water ringed by tea and forest. Part of the classic circuit; pair it with Mattupetty and Kundala on the same drive.

venues.name: Photo Point
venues.note: Exactly what the name promises, a curated bend where a stream runs through rows of tea and tall trees frame the classic postcard of Munnar. Touristy but genuinely photogenic, and a quick, pretty pause on the way in or out of the plantations.

venues.name: Pothamedu Viewpoint
venues.area: 3 km from Munnar town, on the Kochi road
venues.note: One of the great panoramas of the high ranges, undulating tea, cardamom and coffee slopes falling away to a river valley, with the whole Western Ghats stacked in blue layers behind. Close to town, uncrowded, and a favourite of the honeymoon crowd for its sunset light.

venues.name: Attukal Waterfalls
venues.area: Between Pallivasal and Munnar, 9 km from town
venues.note: A frothing white cascade that tumbles over rocks through a wooded gorge, its spray hanging in the tea-country mist, best in and just after the monsoon when it runs full. An easy roadside stop with a short walk to the viewpoint, lovely for photographs on the way into the plantations.

venues.name: Lakkam Waterfalls
venues.note: Fed by the Eravikulam plateau, this fall drops off a rock shelf into a clear pool and is one of the few around Munnar where you can safely dip your feet in a shallow, cordoned bathing area. Set on the Marayoor road, it pairs neatly with a day trip to the sandalwood country.

venues.name: CSI Christ Church (1910)
venues.note: A little stone Anglican church built in 1910 for the British planters, one of the few colonial buildings to survive the catastrophic 1924 floods that redrew Munnar, its worn brass plaques and stained glass still telling the story of the tea pioneers. A serene, ten-minute stop that grounds the whole hill station in its history.

venues.name: Blossom Hydel Park
venues.note: An 18-acre riverside park laid out below the hills, with landscaped walks, cycling tracks, boating and skating, the easy, in-town green space for families with young children. Not the reason you come to Munnar, but a pleasant hour when a multi-generation group wants a gentle morning close to the hotel.

venues.name: The Rose Garden
venues.note: A sprawling hillside garden of roses, fruit orchards and spice plants where you can wander among the beds, watch honey-bees at work and taste estate-grown fruit, a soft, sensory stop that older children and grandparents enjoy. Modest and unhurried; a nice counterpoint to the big viewpoints.

venues.name: Anamudi Shola National Park
venues.note: A compact but precious park of montane shola forest and grassland below Anamudi, threaded with quiet trails and home to Nilgiri tahr, marten and rare shola birds. Far less visited than Eravikulam, it is the one to send a serious walker or birder to for solitude among the mist-forest.
credentials: Western Ghats, UNESCO World Heritage Site

venues.name: Anayirankal Dam & reservoir
venues.note: One of Kerala's largest earthen dams, its still reservoir ringed by tea gardens and evergreen forest, with elephants regularly crossing the far shore, hence the name, 'where elephants descend'. Boating and a picnic on the grassy bank make it a lovely, low-key stop on the Thekkady road.

venues.name: Ethical elephant experience
venues.note: Wild elephants belong to these hills, and the responsible way to meet them is by observation, a naturalist drive through Chinnakanal and Anayirankal where herds cross the tea, rather than the roadside 'rides' the estates now steer guests away from. A good advisor books only welfare-first, observation-based encounters.

venues.name: Sita Devi Lake (Devikulam)
venues.note: A small, mineral-spring lake wrapped in tea slopes and legend, said in the Ramayana to be where Sita bathed, quiet, uncrowded and pretty for a slow walk and a few photographs. A gentle stop for a couple wanting somewhere off the main circuit.

venues.name: Devikulam & the old British plantation trail
venues.note: One of the oldest planter settlements in the hills, its lanes still lined with colonial-era estate bungalows, a little club and mist-wrapped tea gardens, quiet, atmospheric and steeped in the story of British Munnar. Best explored on foot with a guide who knows the planters' history.

venues.name: A stay at Windermere Estate
venues.note: An eighteen-room planter's-bungalow retreat perched on a hilltop inside a working cardamom and coffee estate, with 360-degree views that often look down onto the clouds. The archetypal Munnar tea-country stay, intimate, unhurried, veg-friendly Kerala kitchens and estate walks from the door.

venues.name: A stay at SpiceTree Munnar
venues.note: A boutique retreat of just sixteen suites and pool villas high above Chinnakanal, built for privacy and the long valley views, heated pools, glass-walled rooms in the mist, and elephant country on the doorstep. The choice for a couple or a small family wanting the most polished modern-luxury base in the high ranges.

venues.name: A stay at KTDC Tea County
venues.note: Kerala Tourism's premium hill resort, tucked between two tea-clad hills a short walk from town, with cottages, a spa and easy access to trekking, cycling and the plantations. A reliable, well-located classic for a multi-generation group that wants comfort close to the sights.

venues.name: A guided plantation-country trek
venues.note: The finest way to feel the high ranges is on foot, a half-day walk through tea, shola pockets and grassland ridges with a naturalist, ending at a viewpoint no vehicle reaches. Routes scale from a gentle estate loop for grandparents to a proper ridge hike for teenagers; the estate-stays and forest department both arrange guides.
credentials: Western Ghats, UNESCO World Heritage Site

venues.name: Munnar town market & the tea-and-spice buying
venues.note: The little bazaar in town is where the estate teas, cardamom, pepper, homemade chocolate and eucalyptus oil come together, a good hour to buy genuine single-estate leaf and freshly graded cardamom to carry home. A guide steers you to the honest sellers rather than the tourist-priced stalls.

venues.name: Nyayamakad Waterfalls
venues.area: Between Munnar and Rajamalai, ~10 km from town
venues.note: A long, misty veil of water dropping over a rock face beside the Eravikulam road, at its full glory in and just after the monsoon, an easy roadside pause you pass on the way to the national park. Pretty, uncrowded and perfectly timed with an early Eravikulam visit.

venues.name: Estate bonfire & evening at Windermere Estate
venues.note: The truest Munnar evening, a bonfire and a quiet drink on a plantation hilltop as the mist settles and the temperature drops.
credentials: Plantation-estate evenings at Windermere Estate
Bonfires and terrace drinks in the cool hill air
